title: Oats, whole grain, rolled, old fashioned

content.title: About
content.content: Whole‑grain rolled oats (old fashioned) are made from whole oat kernels that are steamed and then rolled into flat flakes. They retain most of the bran and germ, making them rich in fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals. The flakes have a hearty texture and are ideal for classic oatmeal, baking, and quick‑cook dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats are one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown for over 5,000 years.
Old‑fashioned rolled oats require longer cooking than instant oats but preserve more nutrients.
Oats contain beta‑glucan, a soluble fiber that helps lower cholesterol.
In some regions oats are used as animal feed, but whole‑grain rolled oats are intended for human consumption.
Oats can be grown in temperate climates with relatively low pesticide use.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Beta‑glucan helps reduce LDL‑cholesterol levels, promoting cardiovascular wellness.

items.title: Blood‑sugar regulation
items.content: The fiber slows carbohydrate absorption, leading to more stable post‑meal glucose levels.

items.title: Digestive health
items.content: Both soluble and insoluble fiber improve gut motility and support a healthy microbiome.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Oats provide thiamine (B1), riboflavin (B2), niacin (B3) and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals and antioxidants
items.content: Contains magnesium, iron, zinc and antioxidant avenanthramides that aid overall metabolism.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to oats or oat proteins.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Oats are often processed on equipment shared with wheat, so they may be contaminated with gluten, which matters for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Oats contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in very large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the flakes in water or milk for 5‑10 minutes until tender, use as a base for oatmeal, add to smoothies, bake into cookies, granola, or prepare overnight oats by soaking them in liquid overnight.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store rolled oats in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended shelf life keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.
